name: Puzzles, Tricks & Brain Skills
blurb: Cubes, cards, memory systems and mental arithmetic — the skills that look like magic and are mostly method.

name: Coordination & Dexterity
blurb: Juggling, spinning, shuffling. Pure repetition skills where your hands learn faster than your head.

name: Physical Skills
blurb: Handstands, rope climbs, first pull-ups and fight-sport fundamentals you can train in a corner of a room.

name: Water Skills
blurb: Swimming, surfing, kayaking and the water-safety knowledge that turns open water from a hazard into a place to be.

name: Wheels, Boards & Snow
blurb: Bikes, boards, blades, skis and a manual gearbox — the balance skills that move you, and the one that gets you a hire car anywhere.

name: Outdoor & Survival Skills
blurb: Fire, knots, shelter, water and navigation — the classic competences, each with a clear pass/fail.

name: Garden & Growing
blurb: Seeds, soil, compost and pruning. Nothing here needs a garden — a windowsill and a season will do.

name: First Aid & Safety
blurb: CPR, choking, bleeding, burns and the shutoff valves in your own home. The highest-stakes category on the list.

name: Health & Body Care
blurb: Sleep, posture, teeth, skin and the small maintenance habits that decide how the rest of it feels.

name: Music & Rhythm
blurb: You will not become a musician in three weeks, but you can become genuinely good at one narrow musical thing.

name: Making & Repair Skills
blurb: Sewing, sharpening, soldering, bikes, cars and drywall — the stop-paying-someone-else tier of adulthood.

name: Textile & Fibre Crafts
blurb: Knitting, crochet, embroidery and mending. Slow, portable crafts that turn string into things you actually wear.

name: Cooking & Food Skills
blurb: Knife work, dough, sauces and protein cookery. Practise these and you eat the homework.

name: Social & Performance Skills
blurb: Stories, speeches, names, listening and dancing — trainable skills that most people leave to chance.

name: Language & Script
blurb: Alphabets, pronunciation and the first hundred words — enough of another language to stop being illiterate in it.

name: Writing & Study
blurb: Emails, notes, summaries and how to learn things that stay learned. The skills that make every other skill cheaper.

name: Games & Strategy
blurb: Poker, backgammon, Go and cribbage — games deep enough to keep repaying attention for decades.

name: Animals & Pets
blurb: Training, handling and reading the animals around you, from your own dog to somebody else’s horse.

name: Observation & Awareness Skills
blurb: Learn to read the sky, the trees, the birds and the map. The world gets noisier in a good way.

name: Creative Skills
blurb: Drawing, lettering, folding, carving, shooting and editing — output-based skills with visible weekly progress.

name: Technology Skills
blurb: Typing, the command line, a first website, spreadsheets, Git and sane security hygiene.

name: Money & Everyday Admin
blurb: Budgets, payslips, contracts and scams. Unglamorous, rarely taught, and quietly worth more than most of this list.

name: Navigation & Travel Skills
blurb: Maps, compasses, transit systems and carry-on packing: how to arrive without a blue dot to follow.

name: Precision & Party Skills
blurb: The best effort-to-impressiveness ratio on the whole list. Cards, cues, darts, whips and kendama.

name: Old-School Practical Skills
blurb: Shorthand, slide rules, wax seals, ties, shoeshine and cordage — analogue competence, quietly satisfying.
